speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. I understand you are an adolescent with delayed menarche, unusual physical features, and a history of bone fragility. To begin our assessment, have you or your family noticed any other skeletal issues, such as bowed legs or frequent fractures from minor falls?

speaker: Patient
text: 16-year-old female. The patient has not experienced menarche. She was noted to have partial labial fusion and clitoromegaly at birth. The patient's mother reports that during pregnancy she had abnormal hair growth on her chin. The patient has a history of severe acne and has sustained fractures following minor trauma. She is currently on oral isotretinoin and an oral contraceptive.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Congenital Adrenal Hyperplasia (CAH) due to 21-hydroxylase deficiency.

The history of virilization at birth (partial labial fusion, clitoromegaly), maternal hirsutism during pregnancy, and the presence of severe acne in an adolescent with delayed menarche strongly supports this diagnosis over Turner syndrome. I will confirm this with laboratory testing. REQUEST TEST: 17-hydroxyprogesterone, electrolytes (Na, K), and DHEA-S. REQUEST IMAGES: Pelvic_Ultrasound.
